Create a named locator (cue point) in the Arrangement at a beat position.

    If a locator already exists at that beat (within ~1e-3 tolerance) it is
    renamed instead of toggled off. Time is in beats from the start of the
    arrangement (e.g. 0.0 = start, 16.0 = bar 5 in 4/4).

    Parameters:
    - name: The locator label (e.g. "Chorus", "Verse 1", "Drop")
    - time: Beat position where the locator should sit
    - user_prompt: The original user prompt that led to this tool call (for telemetry)

tools.name: submit_intent
tools.description:
Record the human's creative intent for subsequent actions in this session.

    Call this before a sequence of edits so trajectory steps are conditioned on intent.
    Levels: 1=atomic, 2=musical op, 3=section, 4=song, 5=creative goal.

    Requires telemetry consent. Data is stored in Supabase (same project as telemetry).

    Parameters:
    - text: Natural-language intent (e.g. "make the chorus feel bigger")
    - level: Hierarchical intent level 1–5 (default 5)
    - user_prompt: The original user prompt that led to this tool call (for telemetry)

tools.name: rate_last_action
tools.description:
Rate the most recent recorded action (or the track after an edit).

    Ratings: better | same | worse | keep | reject | thumbs_up | thumbs_down
    Optional tags (comma-separated): groove, harmony, melody, sound, arrangement,
    energy, mix, emotion

    Requires telemetry consent.

    Parameters:
    - rating: Preference label
    - tags: Comma-separated aspect tags
    - note: Optional free-text reason
    - user_prompt: The original user prompt that led to this tool call (for telemetry)

tools.name: prefer_candidate
tools.description:
Record a pairwise preference between two candidate actions or auditions.

    winner should be 'a', 'b', or an explicit candidate id matching A or B.

    Requires telemetry consent.

    Parameters:
    - candidate_a: Id / URI / label for option A
    - candidate_b: Id / URI / label for option B
    - winner: 'a', 'b', or the winning id
    - reason: Optional reason ("C has the right attack")
    - user_prompt: The original user prompt that led to this tool call (for telemetry)

tools.name: reject_last_action
tools.description:
Mark the last action as rejected (exploration / preference boundary).

    Use when the human undoes or discards an agent edit. Requires telemetry consent.

    Parameters:
    - reason: Optional why it was rejected
    - user_prompt: The original user prompt that led to this tool call (for telemetry)

tools.name: record_audition
tools.description:
Log a browser/preset/sample audition (keep or reject) for preference learning.

    Call once per candidate auditioned. Does not load the device — use
    load_instrument_or_effect when kept=True and you want to commit.

    Requires telemetry consent.

    Parameters:
    - uri: Browser item URI (or stable preset/sample id)
    - kept: Whether this candidate was kept
    - search_query: Optional search text that led here (e.g. "analog bass")
    - dwell_ms: Optional time spent auditioning
    - user_prompt: The original user prompt that led to this tool call (for telemetry)

tools.name: search_engine
tools.description: Scrape search results from Google, Bing or Yandex. Returns SERP results in JSON or Markdown (URL, title, description),Ideal forgathering current information, news, and detailed search results.

tools.name: scrape_as_markdown
tools.description: Scrape a single webpage URL with advanced options for content extraction and get back the results in MarkDown language. This tool can unlock any webpage even if it uses bot detection or CAPTCHA.

tools.name: search_engine_batch
tools.description: Run multiple search queries simultaneously. Returns JSON for Google, Markdown for Bing/Yandex.

tools.name: scrape_batch
tools.description: Scrape multiple webpages URLs with advanced options for content extraction and get back the results in MarkDown language. This tool can unlock any webpage even if it uses bot detection or CAPTCHA.

tools.name: discover
tools.description: Search the web and rank results by AI-driven relevance. Returns scored results with title, description, and URL. Supports intent-based ranking, geo-targeting, date filtering, and keyword filtering.

query.description: The search query

intent.description: Describes the specific goal of the search to help the AI evaluate and rank result relevance.If not provided, the query string is used as the intent

country.description: 2-letter ISO country code for localized results (e.g., "US", "GB", "DE")

num_results.description: Exact number of search results to return

filter_keywords.description: Keywords that must appear in search results

start_date.description: Only content updated from this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

end_date.description: Only content updated until this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

tools.name: perplexity_ask
tools.description: Answer a question using web-grounded AI (Perplexity Agent API, fast preset). Best for: quick factual questions, summaries, explanations, and general Q&A. Returns a text response with numbered citations. Fastest and cheapest option. Supports filtering by recency (hour/day/week/month/year), domain restrictions, and search context size. For in-depth multi-source research, use perplexity_research instead. For step-by-step reasoning and analysis, use perplexity_reason instead.

content.description: The content of the message

search_recency_filter.description: Filter search results by recency. Use 'hour' for very recent news, 'day' for today's updates, 'week' for this week, etc.

search_domain_filter.description: Restrict search results to specific domains (e.g., ['wikipedia.org', 'arxiv.org']). Use '-' prefix for exclusion (e.g., ['-reddit.com']).

search_context_size.description: Controls how much web context is retrieved. 'low' is fastest, 'high' provides more comprehensive results.

tools.name: perplexity_research
tools.description: Conduct deep, multi-source research on a topic (Perplexity Agent API, high preset). Best for: literature reviews, comprehensive overviews, investigative queries needing many sources. Returns a detailed response with numbered citations. Significantly slower than other tools (can take minutes). For quick factual questions, use perplexity_ask instead. For logical analysis and reasoning, use perplexity_reason instead.

content.description: The content of the message

tools.name: perplexity_reason
tools.description: Analyze a question using step-by-step reasoning with web grounding (Perplexity Agent API, medium preset). Best for: math, logic, comparisons, complex arguments, and tasks requiring chain-of-thought. Returns a reasoned response with numbered citations. Supports filtering by recency (hour/day/week/month/year), domain restrictions, and search context size. For quick factual questions, use perplexity_ask instead. For comprehensive multi-source research, use perplexity_research instead.

content.description: The content of the message

search_recency_filter.description: Filter search results by recency. Use 'hour' for very recent news, 'day' for today's updates, 'week' for this week, etc.

search_domain_filter.description: Restrict search results to specific domains (e.g., ['wikipedia.org', 'arxiv.org']). Use '-' prefix for exclusion (e.g., ['-reddit.com']).

search_context_size.description: Controls how much web context is retrieved. 'low' is fastest, 'high' provides more comprehensive results.

tools.name: perplexity_search
tools.description: Search the web and return a ranked list of results with titles, URLs, snippets, and dates. Best for: finding specific URLs, checking recent news, verifying facts, discovering sources. Returns formatted results (title, URL, snippet, date) with no AI synthesis. Supports recency filters, domain restrictions, and a lower-latency fast search mode. For AI-generated answers with citations, use perplexity_ask instead.

query.description: Search query string

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-20, default: 10)

max_tokens_per_page.description: Maximum tokens to extract per webpage (default: 1024)

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for regional results (e.g., 'US', 'GB')

search_recency_filter.description: Filter search results by recency. Use 'hour' for very recent news, 'day' for today's updates, 'week' for this week, etc.

search_domain_filter.description: Restrict search results to specific domains (e.g., ['wikipedia.org', 'arxiv.org']). Use '-' prefix for exclusion (e.g., ['-reddit.com']).

search_type.description: Search backend. 'web' (default) is the standard web search. 'fast' is lower latency and lower cost; prefer it for routine lookups inside agent loops, and keep 'web' for rare or ambiguous questions.

tools.name: start_google_auth
tools.description:
Manually initiate Google OAuth authentication flow.

NOTE: This is a legacy OAuth 2.0 tool and is disabled when OAuth 2.1 is enabled.
The authentication system automatically handles credential checks and prompts for
authentication when needed. Only use this tool if:
1. You need to re-authenticate with different credentials
2. You want to proactively authenticate before using other tools
3. The automatic authentication flow failed and you need to retry

In most cases, simply try calling the Google Workspace tool you need - it will
automatically handle authentication if required.

tools.name: search_gmail_messages
tools.description:
Searches messages in a user's Gmail account based on a query.
Returns both Message IDs and Thread IDs for each found message, along with Gmail web interface links for manual verification.
Supports pagination via page_token parameter.

query.description: The search query. Supports standard Gmail search operators.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

page_size.description: The maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 10.

page_token.description: Token for retrieving the next page of results. Use the next_page_token from a previous response.

include_headers.description:
If True, also fetch each message's metadata and include
Subject, From, and Date per result. Costs one metadata get per result,
grouped into HTTP batches of up to 10, plus retries for transient failures.
Defaults to False (output unchanged from prior versions).

tools.name: get_gmail_message_content
tools.description:
Retrieves the full content (subject, sender, recipients, body) of a specific Gmail message.

Bodies are returned inline and truncated at 20,000 characters. Set full=True to
get the complete, untruncated message instead: it is exported to disk and the
response carries a short-lived download URL (HTTP transport) or file path (stdio
transport) rather than the body, so large messages never stream through the model
context. Stateless deployments have no file storage, so there full=True returns the
untruncated body inline.

message_id.description: The unique ID of the Gmail message to retrieve.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

body_format.description: Body output format (only applies when format='full'). 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches the full raw MIME message and returns the base64url-decoded content.

full.description: When True, return the COMPLETE untruncated message: saved to local storage and referenced by download URL/file path instead of the body text, or inlined in the response when the server has no file storage (stateless mode). Use for messages large enough to hit the truncation limit, or when byte-exact fidelity is needed (pair with body_format='raw' for a .eml export).

format.description:
Message format. "full" (default) includes
the body and attachments, "metadata" only headers.

tools.name: get_gmail_messages_content_batch
tools.description:
Retrieves the content of multiple Gmail messages in a single batch request.
Supports up to 25 messages per batch to prevent SSL connection exhaustion.

message_ids.description: List of Gmail message IDs to retrieve (max 25 per batch).

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

format.description: Message format. "full" includes body, "metadata" only headers.

body_format.description: Body output format (only applies when format='full'). 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches the full raw MIME message and returns the base64url-decoded content.

tools.name: get_gmail_attachment_content
tools.description:
Downloads an email attachment and saves it to local disk.

In stdio mode, returns the local file path for direct access.
In HTTP mode, returns a temporary download URL (valid for 1 hour).
May re-fetch message metadata to resolve filename and MIME type.

message_id.description: The ID of the Gmail message containing the attachment.

attachment_id.description: The ID of the attachment to download.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

return_base64.description:
When True, includes the full attachment as a
standard base64 string in the response (in addition to any file
path or download URL). Useful for sandboxed clients that cannot
reach localhost download URLs or the MCP server's local file
paths (e.g. containerized agents with network allowlists). The
returned base64 uses the standard alphabet, so it can be passed
directly to tools like ``draft_gmail_message`` that expect
standard (not URL-safe) base64. Default False preserves the
existing behavior and response size.

attachment_index.description:
Zero-based attachment position from
the message-content response. When the cap is enabled, this lets
the server safely resolve Gmail's refreshed attachment IDs against
current metadata before downloading.

tools.name: send_gmail_message
tools.description:
Sends an email using the user's Gmail account. Supports new emails, replies, and
forwards, with optional attachments. Supports Gmail's "Send As" feature to send
from configured alias addresses.

To forward an existing message, pass forward_message_id. The original subject,
body (quoted with a "Forwarded message" header), and attachments are carried over.
In forward mode, body (if any) is prepended as a note and subject is optional.
Threading, reply, and signature options do not apply when forwarding.

THIS TOOL SENDS IMMEDIATELY AND CANNOT SCHEDULE. Gmail's REST API exposes no
send-time parameter; Schedule send is a web-UI feature with no API equivalent,
so no argument to this tool can defer delivery. Never tell a user a message
was scheduled. For "prepare now, deliver later", create a draft with
draft_gmail_message. An external scheduler must retain the message data to
create and send a new message via send_gmail_message at the chosen time, or
call users.drafts.send with the draft ID returned by draft_gmail_message.
Alternatively, let the user schedule that draft in the Gmail UI.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required for authentication.

to.description: Recipient email address. Optional when replying with reply_all=True, which derives it from the thread.

subject.description: Email subject. Required when sending; optional when forwarding (defaults to 'Fwd: <original subject>').

body.description: Email body content (plain text or HTML). Required when sending. When forwarding, this is an optional note prepended above the quoted original.

body_format.description: Format of the body content (and of the prepended note when forwarding). Use 'plain' for plaintext or 'html' for HTML content.

forward_message_id.description: Set to a Gmail message ID to forward that message instead of composing a new one. The original subject, body, and (optionally) attachments are carried over; 'body' becomes an optional note prepended to the forward.

include_forwarded_attachments.description: When forwarding, whether to include the original message's attachments. Ignored unless forward_message_id is set.

from_name.description: Optional sender display name (e.g., 'Peter Hartree'). If provided, the From header will be formatted as 'Name <email>'.

from_email.description: Optional 'Send As' alias email address. Must be configured in Gmail settings (Settings > Accounts > Send mail as). If not provided, uses the authenticated user's email.

thread_id.description: Optional Gmail thread ID to reply within. When in_reply_to is omitted, replies to the latest non-draft, non-trash message with an RFC Message-ID.

in_reply_to.description: Optional RFC Message-ID to explicitly reply to a specific message (e.g., '<message123@gmail.com>'). Omit to reply to the latest eligible message in thread_id.

references.description: Optional Message-ID ancestry chain. Normally omit when thread_id is provided; the server derives the chain through the selected reply target.

attachments.description: Optional list of attachments. Each can have: "url" (fetch from URL — works with MCP attachment URLs from get_drive_file_download_url / get_gmail_attachment_content), OR "path" (file path, auto-encodes), OR "content" (standard base64, not urlsafe) + "filename". Optional "mime_type". Optional "content_id" (string) makes the attachment inline-rendered: it lands in a multipart/related part with `Content-ID: ` and `Content-Disposition: inline`, and the HTML body can reference it via `` (RFC 2392). Without `content_id` the attachment is a regular multipart/mixed attachment. Example: [{"url": "https://host/attachments/abc-123", "filename": "report.pdf"}]

include_signature.description: Whether to append the Gmail signature from Settings > Signature when available. Defaults to true.

quote_original.description: Whether to include the message being replied to as a quoted original. Only has an effect when thread_id is provided. Defaults to false.

reply_all.description: Whether to derive reply-all recipients from the thread: To = the sender being replied to, Cc = the other participants, excluding the authenticated account and from_email. Requires thread_id. Explicit to/cc win; when cc is omitted the sender being replied to is added to the derived Cc if they are not already in To. Defaults to false.

tools.name: draft_gmail_message
tools.description:
Creates a draft email in the user's Gmail account. Supports both new drafts and reply drafts with optional attachments.
Supports Gmail's "Send As" feature to draft from configured alias addresses.

SCHEDULED SEND IS NOT AVAILABLE. Gmail's REST API exposes no send-time
parameter; the Schedule send feature is web-UI only, and a message cannot be
placed in the Scheduled folder through the API. Do not claim a message was
scheduled. To deliver at a chosen time, create a draft with
draft_gmail_message. An external scheduler must retain the message data to
create and send a new message via send_gmail_message then, or call
users.drafts.send with the draft ID returned by draft_gmail_message.
Alternatively, let the user schedule the draft in the Gmail UI.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required for authentication.

body_format.description: Email body format. Use 'plain' for plaintext or 'html' for HTML content.

from_name.description: Optional sender display name (e.g., 'Peter Hartree'). If provided, the From header will be formatted as 'Name <email>'.

from_email.description: Optional 'Send As' alias email address. Must be configured in Gmail settings (Settings > Accounts > Send mail as). If not provided, uses the account's default Send As address, falling back to the authenticated user's email when Gmail returns no usable Send-As entry or settings access is not authorized.

thread_id.description: Optional Gmail thread ID to reply within. When in_reply_to is omitted, replies to the latest non-draft, non-trash message with an RFC Message-ID.

in_reply_to.description: Optional RFC Message-ID to explicitly reply to a specific message (e.g., '<message123@gmail.com>'). Omit to reply to the latest eligible message in thread_id.

references.description: Optional Message-ID ancestry chain. Normally omit when thread_id is provided; the server derives the chain through the selected reply target.

attachments.description: Optional list of attachments. Each can have: 'url' (fetch from URL — works with MCP attachment URLs from get_drive_file_download_url / get_gmail_attachment_content), OR 'path' (file path, auto-encodes), OR 'content' (standard base64, not urlsafe) + 'filename'. Optional 'mime_type'. Optional 'content_id' (string) makes the attachment inline-rendered: it lands in a multipart/related part with `Content-ID: ` and `Content-Disposition: inline`, and the HTML body can reference it via `` (RFC 2392). Without `content_id` the attachment is a regular multipart/mixed attachment.

include_signature.description: Whether to append the Gmail signature from Settings > Signature when available. Defaults to true.

quote_original.description: Whether to include the original message as a quoted reply. Only has an effect when thread_id is provided. Defaults to false.

tools.name: get_gmail_thread_content
tools.description:
Retrieves the complete content of a Gmail conversation thread, including all messages.

Optionally also returns structured ownership analysis so a caller can
determine who sent the last message and who owes whom a response without
re-parsing the formatted string or making a second tool call.

thread_id.description: The unique ID of the Gmail thread to retrieve.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

body_format.description: Body output format. 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches each message's full raw MIME content and returns the base64url-decoded body.

include_analysis.description: When True, the return value is a dict with both the formatted thread content AND structured ownership analysis (last sender, ball-in-court verdict, per-sender message counts, participants). Defaults to False, in which case the existing string return shape is preserved.

tools.name: get_gmail_threads_content_batch
tools.description:
Retrieves the content of multiple Gmail threads in a single batch request.
Supports up to 25 threads per batch to prevent SSL connection exhaustion.

thread_ids.description: A list of Gmail thread IDs to retrieve. The function will automatically batch requests in chunks of 25.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

body_format.description: Body output format. 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches each message's full raw MIME content and returns the base64url-decoded body.

tools.name: list_gmail_labels
tools.description: Lists labels in the user's Gmail account.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

prefix.description:
Return only labels whose name starts with this
exact (case-sensitive) string. users.labels.list accepts no filter,
so the full list is fetched and narrowed here: this shrinks what the
caller receives, not the API call.

include_system.description:
Include Gmail system labels (INBOX, SENT, ...).
Set False to return user labels only.

tools.name: manage_gmail_label
tools.description: Manages Gmail labels: create, update, or delete labels.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

action.description: Action to perform on the label.

name.description: Label name. Required for create, optional for update.

label_id.description: Label ID. Required for update and delete operations.

label_list_visibility.description: Whether the label is shown in the label list. Defaults to "labelShow" on create. On update, omitting it keeps the label's current setting.

message_list_visibility.description: Whether the label's messages are shown in the message list. Defaults to "show" on create. On update, omitting it keeps the label's current setting.

background_color.description: Label background color as a hex string, e.g. "#fb4c2f". Set together with text_color; Gmail requires both. Gmail accepts only its own palette, and an unsupported value is rejected before the request. Colors apply to user labels, not system labels.

text_color.description: Label text color as a hex string, e.g. "#ffffff". Set together with background_color. Same palette. On update, omitting both keeps the label's current color.

clear_color.description: On update, remove the label's current color. Cannot be combined with background_color or text_color.

tools.name: list_gmail_filters
tools.description: Lists all Gmail filters configured in the user's mailbox.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

tools.name: manage_gmail_filter
tools.description: Manages Gmail filters. Supports creating and deleting filters.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

action.description: Action to perform - "create" or "delete".

filter_action.description: Filter action object (required for create). Named 'filter_action' to avoid shadowing the 'action' parameter.

filter_id.description: ID of the filter to delete (required for delete).

tools.name: modify_gmail_message_labels
tools.description:
Adds or removes labels from a Gmail message.
To archive an email, remove the INBOX label.
To delete an email, add the TRASH label.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

message_id.description: The ID of the message to modify.

add_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to add to the message.

remove_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to remove from the message.

tools.name: batch_modify_gmail_message_labels
tools.description:
Adds or removes labels from multiple Gmail messages in a single batch request.

Takes MESSAGE ids, not thread ids. Gmail's batch endpoint returns no
per-message result and silently ignores ids it does not recognise, so by
default this reads the messages back afterwards and reports which ids
actually changed.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

message_ids.description: A list of message IDs to modify.

add_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to add to the messages.

remove_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to remove from the messages.

verify.description:
Read the messages back and report per-id outcomes. Costs
one extra (batched) read per id. Set False for very large sweeps
where that cost matters and an unverified result is acceptable.

tools.name: search_drive_files
tools.description: Searches for files and folders within a user's Google Drive, including shared drives.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

query.description:
The search query string. Supports Google Drive search operators.
         NOTE: Owner-based queries ('user@example.com' in owners) DO NOT WORK in Shared Drives
         because files are owned by the shared drive itself, not individual users.
         For recent files by a specific user in Shared Drives, search by modifiedTime
         and use order_by='modifiedTime desc' instead.

page_size.description: The maximum number of files to return. Defaults to 10.

page_token.description: Page token from a previous response's nextPageToken to retrieve the next page of results.

drive_id.description: ID of the shared drive to search. If None, behavior depends on `corpora` and `include_items_from_all_drives`.

include_items_from_all_drives.description: Whether shared drive items should be included in results. Defaults to True. This is effective when not specifying a `drive_id`.

corpora.description:
Bodies of items to query (e.g., 'user', 'domain', 'drive', 'allDrives').
                     If 'drive_id' is specified and 'corpora' is None, it defaults to 'drive'.
                     Otherwise, Drive API default behavior applies. Prefer 'user' or 'drive' over 'allDrives' for efficiency.

file_type.description:
Restrict results to a specific file type. Accepts a friendly
                       name ('folder', 'document'/'doc', 'spreadsheet'/'sheet',
                       'presentation'/'slides', 'form', 'drawing', 'pdf', 'shortcut',
                       'script', 'site', 'jam'/'jamboard') or any raw MIME type
                       string (e.g. 'application/pdf'). Defaults to None (all types).

detailed.description: Whether to include size, modified time, and link in results. Defaults to True.

order_by.description:
Sort order. Comma-separated list of sort keys with optional 'desc' modifier.
                      Valid keys: 'createdTime', 'folder', 'modifiedByMeTime', 'modifiedTime',
                      'name', 'name_natural', 'quotaBytesUsed', 'recency', 'sharedWithMeTime',
                      'starred', 'viewedByMeTime'. Example: 'modifiedTime desc' or 'folder,modifiedTime desc,name'.
                      Defaults to None (Drive API default ordering).

include_trashed.description:
Whether to include files in the trash. Defaults to False, matching
                    the Drive web UI and `list_drive_items`. Ignored when `query` already
                    contains its own `trashed` clause (`=` or `!=`), which always wins.

tools.name: get_drive_file_content
tools.description:
Retrieves the content of a specific Google Drive file by ID, supporting files in shared drives.

• Native Google Docs, Sheets, Slides → exported as text / CSV.
• Office files (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx) → unzipped & parsed with std-lib to
  extract readable text.
• PDFs → text extracted with pypdf when possible; scanned/image-only PDFs
  fall back to a download hint.
• Images → returned as base64 with MIME metadata for multimodal clients.
• Any other file → downloaded; tries UTF-8 decode, else notes binary.

user_google_email.description: The user’s Google email address.

tools.name: get_drive_file_download_url
tools.description:
Downloads a Google Drive file and saves it to local disk.

In stdio mode, returns the local file path for direct access.
In HTTP mode, returns a temporary download URL (valid for 1 hour).

For Google native files (Docs, Sheets, Slides), exports to a useful format:
- Google Docs -> PDF (default) or DOCX if export_format='docx'
- Google Sheets -> XLSX (default), PDF if export_format='pdf', or CSV if export_format='csv'
- Google Slides -> PDF (default) or PPTX if export_format='pptx'

For other files, downloads the original file format.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_id.description: The Google Drive file ID to download.

export_format.description:
Optional export format for Google native files.
          Options: 'pdf', 'docx', 'xlsx', 'csv', 'pptx'.
          If not specified, uses sensible defaults (PDF for Docs/Slides, XLSX for Sheets).
          For Sheets: supports 'csv', 'pdf', or 'xlsx' (default).

tools.name: list_drive_items
tools.description:
Lists files/folders or shared drive containers, supporting shared drives.
If `drive_id` is specified, lists items within that shared drive. `folder_id` is then relative to that drive (or use drive_id as folder_id for root).
If `drive_id` is not specified, lists items from user's "My Drive" and accessible shared drives (if `include_items_from_all_drives` is True).
Set `resource_type` to "shared_drives" to list shared drive containers instead of folder contents.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

folder_id.description: The ID of the Google Drive folder. Defaults to 'root'. For a shared drive, this can be the shared drive's ID to list its root, or a folder ID within that shared drive.

page_size.description: The maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 100.

page_token.description: Page token from a previous response's nextPageToken to retrieve the next page of results.

drive_id.description: ID of the shared drive. If provided, the listing is scoped to this drive.

include_items_from_all_drives.description: Whether items from all accessible shared drives should be included if `drive_id` is not set. Defaults to True.

corpora.description: Corpus to query ('user', 'drive', 'allDrives'). If `drive_id` is set and `corpora` is None, 'drive' is used. If None and no `drive_id`, API defaults apply.

file_type.description:
Restrict results to a specific file type. Accepts a friendly
                       name ('folder', 'document'/'doc', 'spreadsheet'/'sheet',

Binary sources may be passed directly as base64_content. On a local server a

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

content.description: Text content for text-based formats. Use only for short snippets or content already in memory.

file_path.description: Local file path or file:// URL for any supported format (MD, TXT, HTML, DOCX, ODT, RTF). Appropriate for larger files than content, but file_path may still load the file into memory or perform non-streaming reads. Avoid very large files that could exceed memory or time limits; use streaming/chunked uploads or an alternative API for huge files.

file_url.description: Remote URL to fetch the file from (http/https).

source_format.description:
Source format hint ('md', 'markdown', 'docx', 'txt', 'html', 'rtf', 'odt').
                           Auto-detected from file_name extension if not provided.

folder_id.description: The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'.

base64_content.description: Standard base64-encoded bytes for a binary source such as DOCX or ODT.

base64_sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 of decoded base64_content. Recommended for binary payload integrity checks.

Imports a presentation (PPTX, PPT, ODP) into Google Slides format with automatic conversion.

file_url.description: Remote URL to fetch the presentation from (http/https).

source_format.description:
Source format hint ('pptx', 'ppt', 'odp').
                           Auto-detected from file_name extension if not provided.

folder_id.description: The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'.

base64_content.description: Standard base64-encoded bytes for a PPTX or ODP source.

base64_sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 of decoded base64_content. Recommended for binary payload integrity checks.

Source format hint ('xlsx', 'xls', 'ods', 'csv', 'tsv').

Gets detailed metadata about a Google Drive file including sharing permissions,

tools.description: Searches for a file by name and checks if it has public link sharing enabled.

file_name.description: The name of the file to check.

ID of the shared drive to scope the search to. When set, the
                      underlying files.list call uses corpora='drive' and the given
                      driveId, which is required to reliably find files that live only
                      in that shared drive. When None, behaviour is unchanged
                      (default API corpora applies).

tools.name: update_drive_file
tools.description:
Updates metadata, properties, and/or content of a Google Drive file.

Providing new content (inline as ``content``, fetched from ``file_url``, or on a
local server read from a file path) replaces the file's content in place,
preserving the existing file ID, sharing, comments, and links.
For native Google Docs/Sheets/Slides the source is uploaded with its source MIME
type so the Drive API applies the same format conversion as import_to_google_doc
(markdown headings, tables, bold, etc.). For any other file (.md, .txt, .pdf, ...)
there is nothing to convert, so the bytes are written back as-is under the file's
own MIME type. Metadata and content can be updated in a single call.

``mode='append'``/``'prepend'`` splice ``content`` onto the file's existing text
server-side, so only the new text has to be supplied — no need to send the whole
file back to rewrite it.

Drive shortcuts are handled according to the kind of update: supported
resource-local metadata changes (rename, move, trash, star, description, and
custom properties) apply to the supplied shortcut, while content replacement
follows the shortcut and updates its target. To avoid applying metadata to the
wrong resource, a shortcut call cannot combine content with resource-local
metadata. Update the shortcut metadata and target content in separate calls.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_id.description: The ID of the file to update. Required.

mime_type.description:
New MIME type (note: changing type may require
content upload). For a shortcut ID, this must accompany content and applies
to the resolved target.

add_parents.description: Comma-separated folder IDs to add as parents.

remove_parents.description: Comma-separated folder IDs to remove from parents.

trashed.description: Whether to move file to/from trash.

writers_can_share.description:
Whether editors can share the file. Pass the
target ID directly; this cannot be changed on a shortcut resource.

copy_requires_writer_permission.description:
Whether copying requires writer
permission. Pass the target ID directly; this cannot be changed on a
shortcut resource.

properties.description: Custom key-value properties for the file.

content.description: New text content for text-based formats (markdown, TXT, HTML).

file_path.description: Local file path for binary formats (DOCX, ODT). Supports file:// URLs.

file_url.description: Remote http(s) URL to fetch new content from.

source_format.description:
Source format hint for conversion
(md, markdown, docx, txt, html, rtf, odt). Auto-detected when omitted, and
ignored for non-Google files, which are uploaded without conversion.
Provide at most one content source.

mode.description:
How to apply the new content — 'replace' (default), 'append', or
'prepend'. Append/prepend require 'content' and a UTF-8 text file such as
.md or .txt; a newline is inserted at the seam if neither side has one.
For native Google Docs use insert_doc_elements, modify_doc_text, or
find_and_replace_doc, which edit in place instead of rewriting the file.

tools.description: Gets the shareable link for a Google Drive file or folder.

tools.name: manage_drive_access
tools.description:
Consolidated tool for managing Google Drive file and folder access permissions.

Supports granting, batch-granting, updating, revoking permissions, and
transferring file ownership -- all through a single entry point.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_id.description: The ID of the file or folder. Required.

action.description:
The access management action to perform. Required. One of:
- "grant": Share with a single user, group, domain, or anyone.
- "grant_batch": Share with multiple recipients in one call.
- "update": Modify an existing permission (role or expiration).
- "revoke": Remove an existing permission.
- "transfer_owner": Transfer file ownership to another user.

share_with.description:
Email address (user/group), domain name (domain),
or omit for 'anyone'. Used by "grant".

role.description:
Permission role -- 'reader', 'commenter', or 'writer'.
Used by "grant" (defaults to 'reader') and "update".

share_type.description:
Type of sharing -- 'user', 'group', 'domain', or 'anyone'.
Used by "grant". Defaults to 'user'.

permission_id.description:
The permission ID to modify or remove.
Required for "update" and "revoke" actions.

recipients.description:
List of recipient objects for
"grant_batch". Each should have: email (str), role (str, optional),
share_type (str, optional), expiration_time (str, optional). For domain
shares use 'domain' field instead of 'email'.

send_notification.description:
Whether to send notification emails. Defaults to True.
Used by "grant" and "grant_batch".

email_message.description:
Custom notification email message.
Used by "grant" and "grant_batch".

expiration_time.description:
Expiration in RFC 3339 format
(e.g., "2025-01-15T00:00:00Z"). Used by "grant" and "update".

allow_file_discovery.description:
For 'domain'/'anyone' shares, whether
the file appears in search. Used by "grant".

new_owner_email.description:
Email of the new owner.
Required for "transfer_owner".

move_to_new_owners_root.description:
Move file to the new owner's My Drive root.
Defaults to False. Used by "transfer_owner".

tools.name: copy_drive_file
tools.description:
Creates a copy of an existing Google Drive file.

This tool copies the template document to a new location with an optional new name.
The copy maintains all formatting and content from the original file.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_id.description: The ID of the file to copy. Required.

new_name.description: New name for the copied file. If not provided, uses "Copy of [original name]".

parent_folder_id.description: The ID of the folder where the copy should be created. Defaults to 'root' (My Drive).

tools.name: set_drive_file_permissions
tools.description:
Sets file-level sharing settings and controls link sharing for a Google Drive file or folder.

This is a high-level tool for the most common permission changes. Use this to toggle
"anyone with the link" access or configure file-level sharing behavior. For managing
individual user/group permissions, use share_drive_file or update_drive_permission instead.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

file_id.description: The ID of the file or folder. Required.

link_sharing.description:
Control "anyone with the link" access for the file.
- "off": Disable "anyone with the link" access for this file.
- "reader": Anyone with the link can view.
- "commenter": Anyone with the link can comment.
- "writer": Anyone with the link can edit.

writers_can_share.description:
Whether editors can change permissions and share.
If False, only the owner can share. Defaults to None (no change).

copy_requires_writer_permission.description:
Whether viewers and commenters
are prevented from copying, printing, or downloading. Defaults to None (no change).

tools.name: list_calendars
tools.description: Retrieves a list of calendars accessible to the authenticated user.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

max_results.description: Maximum calendars to return in one page. Omit to use the API default.

page_token.description: Token for the next page, taken from a previous response.

tools.name: get_events
tools.description:
Retrieves events from a specified Google Calendar. Can retrieve a single event by ID or multiple events within a time range.
You can also search for events by keyword by supplying the optional "query" param.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

calendar_id.description: The ID of the calendar to query. Use 'primary' for the user's primary calendar. Defaults to 'primary'. Calendar IDs can be obtained using `list_calendars`.

event_id.description: The ID of a specific event to retrieve. If provided, retrieves only this event and ignores time filtering parameters.

time_min.description: The start of the time range (inclusive) in RFC3339 format (e.g., '2024-05-12T10:00:00Z' or '2024-05-12'). If omitted, defaults to the current time when single_events=True. It is omitted from unexpanded queries so recurring masters that began in the past but still have future occurrences remain discoverable. Ignored if event_id is provided.

time_max.description: The end of the time range (exclusive) in RFC3339 format. If omitted, events starting from `time_min` onwards are considered (up to `max_results`). Ignored if event_id is provided.

max_results.description: The maximum number of events to return in one page. Defaults to 25. Ignored if event_id is provided.

query.description: A keyword to search for within event fields (summary, description, location). Ignored if event_id is provided.

detailed.description: Whether to return detailed event information including description, location, colour (colorId), attendees, and attendee details (response status, organizer, optional flags). Recurring instances also report the parent series ID needed to edit the whole series; recurring masters report their raw RFC5545 recurrence rules; and events that are not ordinary confirmed meetings report their event type (outOfOffice, workingLocation, focusTime) and status. Defaults to False.

include_attachments.description: Whether to include attachment information in detailed event output. When True, shows attachment details (fileId, fileUrl, mimeType, title) for events that have attachments. Only applies when detailed=True. Set this to True when you need to view or access files that have been attached to calendar events, such as meeting documents, presentations, or other shared files. Defaults to False.

single_events.description: Whether to expand recurring series into individual instances. Defaults to True for backwards compatibility. Set to False with detailed=True to retrieve recurring master events and their exact RFC5545 recurrence rules instead of inferring cadence from expanded instances.

page_token.description: Token for the next page, taken from a previous response. When single_events=True, also pass the response's Pagination time_min as time_min, even if omitted on the first call. Keep all other query parameters unchanged. Ignored if event_id is provided.

tools.name: manage_event
tools.description: Manages calendar events. Supports creating, updating, deleting, and RSVP.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

action.description: Action to perform - "create", "update", "delete", or "rsvp".

start_time.description: Start time (required for create). An RFC3339 UTC offset identifies the exact instant and is preserved. Without an offset, supply start_timezone or timezone. For a local wall-clock time, omit the offset and pass the zone so Google resolves daylight saving; a wrong offset moves the event. Date-only values create all-day events.

end_time.description: End time (required for create). An RFC3339 UTC offset identifies the exact instant and is preserved. Without an offset, supply end_timezone or timezone. All-day end dates are exclusive.

event_id.description: Event ID (required for update and delete).

attendees.description: Attendee email addresses, attendee objects (e.g. {"email": ..., "responseStatus": "accepted"}), or a mix of both.

timezone.description:
IANA timezone applied to both boundaries (e.g.,
"America/New_York"). Converts offset-bearing timestamps without changing their
instant; interprets offset-free timestamps as local times in this zone.
Overridden per boundary by start_timezone/end_timezone.

attachments.description:
List of Google Drive file URLs or IDs to attach.
On action="update" this replaces the event's existing attachments rather than
appending to them, matching the Calendar API's patch semantics.

add_google_meet.description: Whether to add/remove native Google Meet.

conference_data.description:
Raw Google Calendar `conferenceData`
payload to attach a third-party conference (Zoom/Webex/Teams add-on). Use this
for full control; mutually exclusive with the conference_provider helper params
and with add_google_meet. (create/update only)

conference_provider.description:
Higher-level helper: third-party provider name
(e.g. "zoom", "webex", "teams"). Requires conference_uri. The MCP builds the
addOn `conferenceData` block internally. (create/update only)

conference_uri.description:
Join URL for the third-party conference (e.g.
"https://zoom.us/j/123456789"). Required when conference_provider is set.

conference_passcode.description: Optional passcode for the third-party conference.

recurrence.description: RFC5545 recurrence rules for a recurring event, e.g. ["RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=10"].

guests_can_see_other_guests.description: Whether attendees can see other guests.

rsvp_comment.description: Optional message to include with the RSVP response (rsvp action only).

send_updates.description: Notification behavior for create, update, delete, and rsvp — "all" (default), "externalOnly", or "none".

start_timezone.description:
IANA timezone for the start boundary only,
overriding timezone. Use for events whose two ends sit in different zones -
a flight departing 13:45 "Asia/Jerusalem" and landing 17:50
"Europe/Amsterdam" is one event authored in two zones. Explicit timestamp
offsets always preserve the instant, even when the zone differs.

end_timezone.description:
IANA timezone for the end boundary only,
overriding timezone. See start_timezone.

tools.name: manage_out_of_office

Manages Out of Office events on Google Calendar. These special events auto-decline

max_results.description: For "list" action: maximum events to return. Defaults to 10.

calendar_id.description: Calendar ID. Defaults to 'primary'. Focus Time status events live on primary calendars, so use 'primary' or a user's primary calendar ID/email rather than a secondary calendar ID.

tools.name: create_calendar
tools.description: Creates a new secondary Google Calendar.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description:
Searches for Google Docs by name using Drive API (mimeType filter).

Returns:
    str: A formatted list of Google Docs matching the search query.

tools.name: get_doc_content
tools.description:
Retrieves content of a Google Doc or a Drive file (like .docx) identified by document_id.
- Native Google Docs: Fetches content via Docs API.
- Office files (.docx, etc.) stored in Drive: Downloads via Drive API and extracts text.

By default, native Google Docs text is index-aligned with the document:
empty paragraphs are preserved and every non-text element that occupies an
index (inline object, page break, footnote reference, ...) is rendered as one
U+FFFC placeholder per index. The document body starts at index 1, so an
offset n into the text that follows "--- CONTENT ---" is document index n + 1,
and that index can be passed straight to format_text or delete_text. Tables
and multi-tab documents interleave separators, so alignment holds up to the
first table or tab header.

Set preserve_context=True for readable link destinations, internal targets,
smart-chip values, table boundaries, headers, footers, footnotes, and object
context exposed by the Docs API. This output is plain text, not Markdown,
and its offsets must not be used as document editing indices. Comments,
revision history, exact visual layout, and chip details hidden by the API
are not included. Use get_doc_as_markdown for formatting or comments.

user_google_email.description: User's Google email address

document_id.description: ID of the Google Doc (or full URL)

suggestions_view_mode.description:
How to render suggestions in the returned content:
- "DEFAULT_FOR_CURRENT_ACCESS": Default based on user's access level
- "SUGGESTIONS_INLINE": Suggested changes appear inline in the document
- "PREVIEW_SUGGESTIONS_ACCEPTED": Preview as if all suggestions were accepted
- "PREVIEW_WITHOUT_SUGGESTIONS": Preview as if all suggestions were rejected

tab_id.description:
Optional ID of a single tab to read (from inspect_doc_structure).
When given, only that tab's content is returned with no tab separator,
so the default output stays index-aligned with that tab. When
omitted, every tab is returned with "--- TAB: ... ---" markers.

preserve_context.description:
Include readable semantic annotations for native Docs.
Defaults to False to retain index alignment. Office extraction is
unaffected. With tab_id, only the selected tab is rendered.

tools.name: list_docs_in_folder
tools.description:
Lists Google Docs within a specific Drive folder.

To avoid index calculation errors, build documents in phases:

  Append text, section breaks, and page breaks sequentially.
  Each operation appends to the end of the body. No index needed.
  Example batch: [
    {"type": "insert_text", "end_of_segment": true, "text": "Report Title\n"},
    {"type": "insert_text", "end_of_segment": true, "text": "\nExecutive Summary\n"},
    {"type": "insert_text", "end_of_segment": true, "text": "Revenue grew 15%.\n"},
    {"type": "insert_section_break", "end_of_segment": true, "section_type": "NEXT_PAGE"},
    {"type": "insert_text", "end_of_segment": true, "text": "Detailed Analysis\n"}
  ]

PHASE 2 - CREATE HEADERS/FOOTERS (if needed):
  For normal header/footer text, use update_doc_headers_footers
  (it auto-creates if missing and writes the content for you).
  Only include create_header_footer operations in a batch when you are
  intentionally managing advanced section-break-specific layouts.

tools.name: inspect_doc_structure
tools.description:
Essential tool for finding safe insertion points and understanding document structure.

USE THIS FOR:
- Finding the correct index for table insertion
- Understanding document layout before making changes
- Locating existing tables and their positions
- Getting document statistics and complexity info
- Inspecting structure of specific tabs

CRITICAL FOR TABLE OPERATIONS:
ALWAYS call this BEFORE creating tables to get a safe insertion index.

WHAT THE OUTPUT SHOWS:
- total_elements: Number of document elements
- total_length: Maximum safe index for insertion
- tables: Number of existing tables
- table_details: Position and dimensions of each table
- headers / footers: Real segment IDs and previews for header/footer editing
- tabs: List of available tabs in the document (if no tab_id specified)
- empty_paragraphs: newline-only count, excluding existing/suggested object anchors
- empty_paragraph_ranges: start/end extents, capped at 100
- empty_paragraph_ranges_truncated: whether ranges were omitted
- last_paragraph: is_list_item and is_empty, or null if no body paragraphs

Paragraph statistics cover top-level body paragraphs and appear at the top
level in basic mode or under "statistics" in detailed mode.
Ranges can include required empty paragraphs. Before cleanup, use detailed=true
to check adjacent elements, formatting, and object anchors. Preserve the final
newline and newlines before tables, tables of contents, or section breaks.
The final range has end == total_length and may be omitted by truncation.

WORKFLOW FOR TABLE INSERTION:
Step 1: Call this function
Step 2: Note the "total_length" value
Step 3: Use an index < total_length for table insertion
Step 4: Create your table

FORMATTING WORKFLOW:
After inserting all text via batch_update_doc with end_of_segment=true,
call this tool with detailed=true to get exact start_index and end_index
for every paragraph. Use those indices directly in format_text and
update_paragraph_style operations in a second batch_update_doc call.

HEADER/FOOTER WORKFLOW:
For ordinary header/footer text, use update_doc_headers_footers.
If you need low-level segment editing, call this tool first and use the
real segment_id values returned under headers/footers. Do not invent IDs.

The detailed output includes elements[].start_index and elements[].end_index
with text_preview for each paragraph, making it easy to identify which
ranges to format.

SUB-PARAGRAPH FORMATTING:
text_preview is truncated to 100 characters by default. To compute the index
of a token inside a longer paragraph, pass preview_chars=0 or None for untruncated
text, then add the token's UTF-16 offset within that text to the paragraph's
start_index (non-BMP characters such as emoji occupy two UTF-16 units).

user_google_email.description: User's Google email address

document_id.description: ID of the document to inspect

detailed.description: Whether to return detailed structure information

tab_id.description: Optional ID of the tab to inspect. If not provided, inspects main document.

preview_chars.description:
Maximum characters of paragraph, header and footer text
preview. Pass 0 or None for the full text, needed to locate a token inside a
paragraph longer than the default 100 characters.

tools.name: create_table_with_data
tools.description:
Creates a table and populates it with data in one reliable operation.

CRITICAL: YOU MUST CALL inspect_doc_structure FIRST TO GET THE INDEX!

MANDATORY WORKFLOW - DO THESE STEPS IN ORDER:

Step 1: ALWAYS call inspect_doc_structure first
Step 2: Use the 'total_length' value from inspect_doc_structure as your index
Step 3: Format data as 2D list: [["col1", "col2"], ["row1col1", "row1col2"]]
Step 4: Call this function with the correct index and data

EXAMPLE DATA FORMAT:
table_data = [
    ["Header1", "Header2", "Header3"],    # Row 0 - headers
    ["Data1", "Data2", "Data3"],          # Row 1 - first data row
    ["Data4", "Data5", "Data6"]           # Row 2 - second data row
]

CRITICAL INDEX REQUIREMENTS:
- NEVER use index values like 1, 2, 10 without calling inspect_doc_structure first
- ALWAYS get index from inspect_doc_structure 'total_length' field
- Index must be a valid insertion point in the document

DATA FORMAT REQUIREMENTS:
- Must be 2D list of strings only
- Each inner list = one table row
- All rows MUST have same number of columns
- Use empty strings "" for empty cells, never None
- Use debug_table_structure after creation to verify results

user_google_email.description: User's Google email address

document_id.description: ID of the document to update

bold_headers.description: Whether to make first row bold (default: true)

Number of leading rows to mark as a repeating header that
reappears after each page break. Must be between 0 and the number of

tools.name: debug_table_structure
tools.description:
ESSENTIAL DEBUGGING TOOL - Use this whenever tables don't work as expected.

USE THIS IMMEDIATELY WHEN:
- Table population put data in wrong cells
- You get "table not found" errors
- Data appears concatenated in first cell
- Need to understand existing table structure
- Planning to use populate_existing_table

WHAT THIS SHOWS YOU:
- Exact table dimensions (rows × columns)
- Each cell's position coordinates (row,col)
- Current content in each cell
- Insertion indices for each cell
- Table boundaries and ranges

HOW TO READ THE OUTPUT:
- "dimensions": "2x3" = 2 rows, 3 columns
- "position": "(0,0)" = first row, first column
- "current_content": What's actually in each cell right now
- "insertion_index": Where new text would be inserted in that cell

WORKFLOW INTEGRATION:
1. After creating table → Use this to verify structure
2. Before populating → Use this to plan your data format
3. After population fails → Use this to see what went wrong
4. When debugging → Compare your data array to actual table structure

TEXT_CONTAINS, DATE_BEFORE, CUSTOM_FORMULA). Required for "add".
Optional for "update" (preserves existing type if omitted).

condition_values.description:
Values
for the condition; accepts a list or a JSON string representing a list.
Depends on condition_type. Used by "add" and "update".

background_color.description:
Hex background color to apply when
condition matches. Used by "add" and "update".

text_color.description:
Hex text color to apply when condition matches.
Used by "add" and "update".

rule_index.description:
0-based index of the rule. For "add", optionally
specifies insertion position. Required for "update" and "delete".

gradient_points.description:
List (or JSON list) of
gradient points for a color scale. If provided, a gradient rule is created
and boolean parameters are ignored. Used by "add" and "update".

sheet_name.description:
Sheet name to locate the rule when range_name is
omitted. Defaults to the first sheet. Used by "update" and "delete".

tools.name: create_spreadsheet
tools.description: Creates a new Google Spreadsheet.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

title.description: The title of the new spreadsheet. Required.

sheet_names.description: List of sheet names to create. If not provided, creates one sheet with default name.

folder_id.description:
The ID of the parent folder. Defaults to 'root'. For shared
drives, this must be a folder ID within the shared drive.

tools.name: create_sheet
tools.description: Creates a new sheet or duplicates an existing sheet (user_google_email: str, spreadsheet_id: str, sheet_name: Optional[str] = None, source_sheet_name: Optional[str] = None, insert_sheet_index: Optional[int] = None).

tools.name: list_sheet_tables
tools.description:
Lists all structured tables in a spreadsheet with their IDs, names, ranges,
and column details. Use this to find table IDs for append_table_rows.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

tools.name: append_table_rows
tools.description:
Appends rows to a structured table in a Google Sheet. The rows are added
to the end of the table body, automatically extending the table range.

Use list_sheet_tables first to find the table ID.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

table_id.description: The ID of the table to append to (get from list_sheet_tables). Required.

values.description:
2D array of values to append. Each inner
list is one row. Can be a JSON string or Python list. Required.

tools.name: manage_sheet_tab
tools.description:
Manages the lifecycle of an existing sheet tab: rename, delete, hide, unhide or reorder.

Use create_sheet to add a tab, and resize_sheet_dimensions for row and column
level changes. This tool operates on the tab itself.

user_google_email.description: User's Google email address

sheet_name.description: Title of the existing tab to act on

action.description: One of "rename", "delete", "hide", "unhide", "reorder"

new_index.description: New zero-based position, required for action="reorder"

tools.name: resize_sheet_dimensions
tools.description:
Manages sheet-level dimension properties: resize columns/rows, auto-resize
to fit content, freeze rows/columns, hide/unhide rows/columns, and
insert/delete rows/columns.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

sheet_name.description:
Sheet name to target. Defaults to the
first sheet if not provided.

column_sizes.description:
Dict mapping column letters
to pixel widths. Example: {"A": 200, "C": 300}. Can be a JSON
string or Python dict.

row_sizes.description:
Dict mapping 1-based row
numbers to pixel heights. Example: {"1": 40, "3": 60}. Can be
a JSON string or Python dict.

auto_resize_columns.description:
List of column
letters to auto-resize to fit content. Example: ["A", "B"].

auto_resize_rows.description:
List of 1-based
row numbers to auto-resize to fit content. Example: [1, 2].

frozen_row_count.description:
Number of rows to freeze from the
top. Use 0 to unfreeze all rows.

frozen_column_count.description:
Number of columns to freeze from
the left. Use 0 to unfreeze all columns.

hide_columns.description:
List of column letters
to hide. Example: ["C", "D"].

unhide_columns.description:
List of column
letters to unhide. Example: ["C", "D"].

hide_rows.description:
List of 1-based row
numbers to hide. Example: [3, 4].

unhide_rows.description:
List of 1-based row
numbers to unhide. Example: [3, 4].

insert_rows_at.description:
1-based row number to insert before.
Appends to the end of the sheet if omitted.

insert_columns_at.description:
Column letter to insert before
(e.g. "C"). Appends to the end if omitted.

delete_rows.description:
List of 1-based row
numbers to delete. Example: [5, 6]. Best for non-contiguous rows.

delete_row_range.description:
Contiguous range of rows to delete,
as "start:end" (1-based, inclusive). Example: "5:10" deletes rows
5 through 10. More efficient than delete_rows for large contiguous
ranges.

delete_columns.description:
List of column
letters to delete. Example: ["E", "F"].

tools.name: move_sheet_rows
tools.description:
Moves rows from one sheet to another within the same spreadsheet. The move
is performed in a single batchUpdate (copyPaste followed by
deleteDimension). Note: batchUpdate executes requests sequentially but does
not roll back on partial failure — if the copy succeeds but the delete
fails, rows may be duplicated. Formulas, data types, and formatting are
preserved (unlike a values.get/append round-trip).
Row numbers are 1-based (matching the spreadsheet UI).

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

source_sheet.description: Name of the sheet to move rows from. Required.

start_row.description: First row to move (1-based, inclusive). Required.

end_row.description: Last row to move (1-based, inclusive). Required.

destination_sheet.description: Name of the sheet to move rows to. Required.

tools.name: manage_named_range
tools.description: Manages the lifecycle of named ranges in a Google Sheet: list, create, update, or delete.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

spreadsheet_id.description: The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.

action.description: The operation to perform: "list", "create", "update", or "delete". Required.

name.description: Name for the named range (required for "create"; optional identifier for "update"/"delete").

range_name.description: Target cell or range in A1 notation (e.g., "Sheet1!A1:D10", "A1:B5") (required for "create").

named_range_id.description: The ID of the named range (optional identifier for "update"/"delete").

new_name.description: New name for the named range (used with action="update").

new_range.description: New A1-style range for the named range (used with action="update").

    Sheets comments are cell-scoped via the API.
  - reply: Reply to a comment. Requires comment_id and comment_content.
  - resolve: Resolve a comment. Requires comment_id.

tools.name: list_spaces
tools.description:
Lists Google Chat spaces (rooms and direct messages) accessible to the user.

Returns:
    str: A formatted list of Google Chat spaces accessible to the user.

tools.name: get_messages
tools.description: Retrieves messages from a Google Chat space.

message_filter.description:
Optional filter string using the Chat API filter syntax.
            Supports createTime and thread.name.
            Examples:
              'createTime > "2026-03-18T00:00:00-03:00"'
              'createTime > "2026-03-18T00:00:00-03:00" AND createTime < "2026-03-19T00:00:00-03:00"'
              'thread.name = spaces/X/threads/Y'

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Sends a message to a Google Chat space, or edits a message already sent there.

thread_key.description: Reply in a thread by app-defined key (creates thread if not found).

thread_name.description: Reply in an existing thread by its resource name (e.g. spaces/X/threads/Y).

message_name.description:
Edit this message in place instead of sending a new one
(e.g. spaces/X/messages/Y, as returned by send_message or get_messages).
Must be a message of space_id. Only the text is replaced, and only the
author can edit their own message.

tools.name: search_messages
tools.description: Searches for messages in Google Chat spaces by text content and/or time range.

query.description: Optional text to search for. If omitted, only time_filter is applied.

space_id.description: Optional space to restrict the search to.

page_size.description: Maximum number of messages to return per space.

time_filter.description:
Optional filter using Chat API createTime syntax.
         Examples:
           'createTime > "2026-03-18T00:00:00-03:00"'
           'createTime > "2026-03-18T00:00:00-03:00" AND createTime < "2026-03-19T00:00:00-03:00"'

max_spaces.description: Maximum number of spaces to search when space_id is not provided (default 10).

tools.name: create_reaction
tools.description: Adds an emoji reaction to a Google Chat message.

emoji_unicode.description: The emoji character to react with (e.g. 👍).

tools.name: download_chat_attachment
tools.description:
Downloads an attachment from a Google Chat message and saves it to local disk.

In stdio mode, returns the local file path for direct access.
In HTTP mode, returns a temporary download URL (valid for 1 hour).

attachment_index.description: Zero-based index of the attachment to download (default 0).

tools.name: batch_update_form
tools.description:
Apply batch updates to a Google Form.

Supports adding, updating, and deleting form items, as well as updating
form metadata and settings. This is the primary method for modifying form
content after creation.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

form_id.description: The ID of the form to update.

List of update requests to apply.
Supported request types:
- createItem: Add a new question or content item
- updateItem: Modify an existing item
- deleteItem: Remove an item
- moveItem: Reorder an item
- updateFormInfo: Update form title/description
- updateSettings: Modify form settings (e.g., quiz mode)

tools.name: create_presentation
tools.description: Create a new Google Slides presentation.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

title.description: The title for the new presentation. Defaults to "Untitled Presentation".

tools.name: get_presentation
tools.description: Get details about a Google Slides presentation.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

presentation_id.description: The ID of the presentation to retrieve.

include_speaker_notes.description:
Also report each slide's speaker (presenter)
notes and the object ID of the shape holding them. Pass True when you
need to read or edit notes: that shape ID is the only valid target for
insertText/deleteText on notes, and batch_update_presentation writes
notes by deleting the shape's existing text and inserting new text.
Defaults to False.

include_geometry.description:
Also list each slide's elements with their
placement - transform (translate, and scale/shear when not identity)
and intrinsic size, in raw EMU. Set this when adding slides to an
existing deck so new elements can match its established margins and
content width. Defaults to False.

tools.name: batch_update_presentation
tools.description: Apply batch updates to a Google Slides presentation.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

presentation_id.description: The ID of the presentation to update.

requests.description: List of update requests to apply.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Get details about a specific page (slide) in a presentation.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

page_object_id.description: The object ID of the page/slide to retrieve.

include_geometry.description:
Also report each element's placement - its
transform (translate, and scale/shear when not identity) and intrinsic
size, in raw EMU. Set this when adding elements to an existing deck:
it is the only way to discover the deck's margins, gutters and content
width, which Slides exposes nowhere else, and it reports the same terms
batch_update_presentation writes. Defaults to False to keep the
default output's token cost unchanged.

tools.name: get_page_thumbnail
tools.description: Generate a thumbnail URL for a specific page (slide) in a presentation.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

page_object_id.description: The object ID of the page/slide.

task_list_id.description: The ID of the task list to retrieve tasks from.

max_results.description: Maximum number of tasks to return. (default: 20, max: 10000).

show_completed.description: Whether to include completed tasks (default: True). Note that show_hidden must also be true to show tasks completed in first party clients, such as the web UI and Google's mobile apps.

completed_min.description: Lower bound for completion date (RFC 3339 timestamp).

due_max.description: Upper bound for due date (RFC 3339 timestamp).

due_min.description: Lower bound for due date (RFC 3339 timestamp).

task_list_id.description: The ID of the task list. Required for all actions.

tools.description:
Create, update, or delete a contact. Consolidated tool replacing create_contact,
update_contact, and delete_contact.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

action.description: The action to perform: "create", "update", or "delete".

contact_id.description: The contact ID. Required for "update" and "delete" actions.

items.description: Typed input for a phone entry.

value.description: Backward-compatible alias for the phone number value.

type.description: Phone type such as mobile, work, home, or internal.

phones.description:
List of phone dicts {number, type?}.
Supported types: mobile, work, home, main, workMobile, internal, other, etc.
Use type="internal" for internal PBX/ATS short numbers (e.g. 250, 301) — stored
as a standalone number without + prefix, displayed as "Internal: 250".

items.description: Typed input for an email entry.

value.description: Backward-compatible alias for the email address value.

type.description: Email type such as work, home, or other.

items.description: Typed input for an organization entry.

type.description: Organization type such as work or school.

organizations.description: List of org dicts {name?, title?, department?, jobDescription?, type?}.

items.description: Typed input for a nickname entry.

value.description: Nickname value. Used for bilingual contacts (e.g. Hebrew alternative form).

type.description: Nickname type such as default, alternate_name, maiden_name, initials, or other.

nicknames.description:
List of nickname dicts {value, type?}.
Useful for bilingual contacts (e.g. Hebrew/English alternative forms). Android dialer
and WhatsApp search both index nicknames, enabling cross-script lookup.
Supported types: default, alternate_name, maiden_name, initials, other, etc.

items.description: Typed input for a URL entry.

value.description: The URL value (e.g. https://example.com).

type.description: URL type such as homepage, blog, profile, work, ftp, reservations, or other. Custom values allowed.

urls.description:
List of URL dicts {value, type?}.
Supported types: homepage, blog, profile, work, ftp, reservations, other, etc.

items.description: Typed input for a userDefined custom field entry.

value.description: Custom field value. May be omitted when using remove mode (only the key is needed).

user_defined.description:
List of custom field dicts {key, value}.
Useful for structured data like account numbers, IDs, or custom dates.

items.description: Typed input for a relation entry (spouse, parent, child, etc.).

person.description: The related person's name (matched against contact names by Google Assistant).

type.description: Relation type: spouse, child, parent, father, mother, sister, brother, friend, manager, assistant, partner, sibling, domesticPartner, or custom.

relations.description:
List of relation dicts {person, type?}.
Supported types: spouse, child, parent, friend, manager, assistant, etc.

birthday.description: Birthday as 'YYYY-MM-DD', 'MM-DD' (no year), or 'clear'/'' to remove.

phones_mode.description:
How to update phones on "update": "merge" (default), "replace", or "remove".
merge = read-modify-write with dedup by canonicalForm/normalized value.
replace = overwrite all phones with provided list.
remove = delete phones matching provided numbers.

emails_mode.description: How to update emails on "update": "merge" (default), "replace", or "remove".

organizations_mode.description: How to update orgs on "update": "merge" (default), "replace", or "remove".

nicknames_mode.description: How to update nicknames on "update": "merge" (default), "replace", or "remove".

urls_mode.description:
How to update urls on "update": "merge" (default), "replace", or "remove".
merge dedups by normalized URL (lowercased, trailing slash stripped).

user_defined_mode.description:
How to update custom fields on "update": "merge" (default), "replace", or "remove".
merge overrides value on matching key; new keys appended.

relations_mode.description: How to update relations on "update": "merge" (default), "replace", or "remove".
